ASQ Suicide Risk Screening — FHIR Questionnaire Template

NIMH screen for suicide risk in medical settings: screening questions, the acuity question asked after a positive answer, and the published result and next steps.

Open in Builder

Scoring

A Yes to any of the screening questions is a positive screen. The acuity question then separates an acute positive screen from a non-acute one; all No is a negative screen.

Questions

  1. In the past few weeks, have you wished you were dead?
    • Yes
    • No
  2. In the past few weeks, have you felt that you or your family would be better off if you were dead?
    • Yes
    • No
  3. In the past week, have you been having thoughts about killing yourself?
    • Yes
    • No
  4. Have you ever tried to kill yourself?
    • Yes
    • No
  5. If yes, when was the most recent attempt?
    • Within last 12 months
    • Over 1 year ago
  6. Are you having thoughts of killing yourself right now?
    • Yes
    • No

Calculated results

  • Screening result and next steps

Source and license

Source: Horowitz et al. 2012, Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 166:1170 (ASQ); NIMH Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ) Toolkit. Codes: LOINC. (link)

License: Public domain tool, free of charge (per the NIMH ASQ Toolkit information sheet; developed at the NIMH Intramural Research Program). (link)

Provided to save authoring effort, not as medical advice — confirm the scale and its cut-offs for your use case.

Use it

  1. Download the FHIR Questionnaire JSON, or
  2. open it in the Builder right away (or open the Builder, choose + Add → From template… and search for “ASQ Suicide Risk Screening”). It arrives as one titled group with its calculations wired, and you can keep editing it.
